notes.subject: Reasoning
notes.topic: Syllogism
notes.content: Syllogism involves deriving conclusions from given statements. Always follow: All A are B → Some B are A (converse). No A is B → No B is A. Some A are B → Some B are A. Key tip: Use Venn diagrams for accuracy.
key_points: Universal Positive: All A are B
Universal Negative: No A is B
Particular Positive: Some A are B
Particular Negative: Some A are not B
Always draw Venn diagrams to eliminate wrong choices
notes.example: Statements: All cats are dogs. Some dogs are rats. Conclusion: Some rats are cats → FALSE. Some cats are dogs → TRUE (conversion of first statement)

notes.subject: Reasoning
notes.topic: Blood Relations
notes.content: Blood relation questions test family tree understanding. Always draw a family tree while solving. Key relationships: Father's father = Paternal Grandfather. Mother's brother = Maternal Uncle.
key_points: Always draw a family tree diagram
Identify gender from terms used
+Generation = elder, -Generation = younger
Avoid assumptions — go only by given info
notes.example: A is B's sister. B is C's brother. C is D's son. D is a woman. → A is D's daughter.

notes.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
notes.topic: Percentage
notes.content: Percentage is a ratio expressed as a fraction of 100. Core formula: Percentage = (Part/Whole) × 100. Used in profit/loss, discount, tax, and data interpretation.
key_points: x% of y = y% of x (symmetry trick)
% increase = (new - old)/old × 100
% decrease = (old - new)/old × 100
Successive % change: a% then b% = a + b + ab/100
notes.example: If price increases from ₹500 to ₹600: % increase = (100/500)×100 = 20%

notes.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
notes.topic: Simple & Compound Interest
notes.content: Interest is the extra money paid on a principal amount. SI grows linearly, CI grows exponentially. CI is always ≥ SI for same P, R, T.
key_points: SI = PRT/100
CI - SI for 2 years = PR²/10000
If CI is half-yearly: R becomes R/2, T becomes 2T

notes.subject: English
notes.topic: Tenses
notes.content: Tenses indicate the time of action. There are 3 main tenses (Past, Present, Future), each with 4 aspects (Simple, Continuous, Perfect, Perfect Continuous) = 12 tenses total.
key_points: Simple Present: V1/V1+s/es (He goes)
Present Continuous: is/am/are + V-ing (She is going)
Present Perfect: has/have + V3 (They have gone)
Past Simple: V2 (He went)
Future Simple: will/shall + V1 (She will go)
notes.example: I study every day (Simple Present). I am studying now (Present Continuous). I have studied (Present Perfect).

notes.subject: English
notes.topic: Reading Comprehension Strategy
notes.content: RC passages test your ability to understand, infer, and evaluate written text. A strategic approach saves time and improves accuracy significantly.
key_points: Skim the passage first (30 seconds) to get the gist
Read all questions before reading in detail
For 'tone' questions: identify positive/negative/neutral
Eliminate extreme answer choices (always, never, only)
Vocabulary in context: use surrounding sentences
notes.example: If asked 'What is the author's main purpose?' — look for the central argument, not a detail. Usually stated in first or last paragraph.

notes.subject: General Awareness
notes.topic: Indian Constitution — Key Articles
notes.content: The Indian Constitution is the supreme law of India. It has 448 articles, 25 parts, and 12 schedules. Knowing key articles is essential for all competitive exams.
key_points: Article 14: Right to Equality
Article 19: Right to Freedom (6 freedoms)
Article 21: Right to Life and Personal Liberty
Article 32: Right to Constitutional Remedies (Heart of Constitution)
Article 356: President's Rule (State Emergency)
Article 370: (Abrogated in 2019) — J&K special status

notes.subject: General Awareness
notes.topic: Important Banking Terms
notes.content: Banking terminology is crucial for Banking and SSC exams. These terms appear in both objective and descriptive questions.
key_points: Repo Rate: Rate at which RBI lends to commercial banks
Reverse Repo: Rate at which RBI borrows from banks
CRR (Cash Reserve Ratio): % of deposits banks keep with RBI
SLR (Statutory Liquidity Ratio): % in liquid assets
NPA: Non-Performing Asset (loan not repaid for 90+ days)
RTGS: Real Time Gross Settlement (min ₹2 lakh)
notes.example: If RBI increases Repo Rate → banks borrow at higher cost → loans become expensive → inflation cools down.

notes.subject: Reasoning
notes.topic: Series Completion — Number & Letter
notes.content: Series questions involve identifying the pattern and finding the missing term. Patterns can be arithmetic, geometric, alternating, prime-based, or square/cube-based.
key_points: Check differences first (arithmetic/geometric)
If differences don't work — try squares, cubes, primes
Alternating series: check odd and even positions separately
Letter series: convert letters to numbers (A=1, Z=26)
Mixed series: look for two interleaved patterns

notes.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
notes.topic: Time, Speed and Distance
notes.content: TSD problems are fundamental in all competitive exams. The relationship: Distance = Speed × Time. Always convert units to the same system before solving.
key_points: 1 km/hr = 5/18 m/s | 1 m/s = 18/5 km/hr
Average speed = 2xy/(x+y) when distances are equal
Relative speed: same dir = |a-b|, opp dir = a+b
Train problems: Length of train must be added to distance
notes.example: A train 200m long passes a 400m bridge at 60 km/hr. Time = 600m ÷ (60×5/18) m/s = 600÷16.67 = 36 seconds.
